We can add more clients as they're ready. <@845691100072509460> I've been using your local devnet kurtosis setup. I've suddenly started running into an issue that I'm not familiar with: ``` make run-registry kurtosis run github.com/ethpandaops/ethereum-package --enclave bals --args-file ./kurtosis.config.registry.yaml --image-download always There was an error interpreting Starlark code Evaluation error: fail: perfect_peerdas_enabled is true (this is a unique test if you don't know what it does, consider removing it) but the number of participants (2) is less than 16. Please set the number of participants to at least 16. at [github.com/ethpandaops/ethereum-package/main.star:79:57]: run at [github.com/ethpandaops/ethereum-package/src/package_io/input_parser.star:320:21]: input_parser at [0:0]: fail Error encountered running Starlark code. ``` any idea how to get around this? seems like it might be impossible to get it working without having 16 nodes in the local setup.... because apparently we need to do that to enable fulu. I've just updated configs, could you try it again? perfect_peerdas should not be enabled its a special test case Yeah instead set `supernode: true` for all participants, otherwise in smaller networks you wont have enough custody columns (but i think eth-pkg does this automatically for smaller networks now) works with the fix from jihoon this is a different issue, updated the image with a fix `ethpandaops/lodestar:bal-devnet-0-77fda95` so geth *should* be ready for a devnet now. It's at least stable in a local geth-only devnet configuration. I've updated the `bal-devnet-0` branch on the geth repo. can you remove the amsterdam requirement in the blobschedule? <https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/688075293562503241/1425748011438575719> Did you tried in a network also with Besu / Geth / Reth to see where is the issue ? It's a block created by Reth or Besu ? geth didn't work yesterday in a geth only network so i only tried besu and reth in the same network as both besu and reth managed to get past gloas fork in their own homogeneous network reth does not accept the bal hash from besu and same other way round I think when Geth is working again having a network with the 3 clients at the same time will help to find where is the difference . block 32 seems to be easy to trigger a mismatch Is Reth passing last version of BAL tests ? I can't test a nethermind only network with kurtosis getting the following error (using the following config FULU FORK is set to epoch 0): ``` "eip7928TransitionTimestamp": "0x68e7b6f7", "blobSchedule": [ { "timestamp": "0x0", "target": 6, "max": 9, "baseFeeUpdateFraction": "0x4c6964" } ] ``` could someone from nethermind have a look Hey <@577788234810130432> please could you check which commit you are running on? ```

```
kurtosis run github.com/ethpandaops/ethereum-package --enclave bals --args-file ./kurtosis.config.registry.yaml --image-download always

```
